messages:
Leila (People Ops): Quick heads-up — we've published a short-term PTO advance policy and a fallback staffing playbook for teams covering unexpected absences. TL;DR: if someone needs immediate paid time off and doesn't have accrual, they can request an advance (up to 5 days) and teams should follow the fallback staffing steps listed below. Link: https://intranet.redwood/people/pto-advance

Marcus (HRBP): Nice, when does this take effect?

Leila (People Ops): Effective immediately for operational emergencies (family medical, bereavement, urgent travel). Formal eligibility & exceptions in the doc — but managers can approve advances for up to 5 days, payroll will recoup via future accruals or a one-time payroll adjustment (employee choice).

Jin (Eng Manager): For planning: what's the expected manager turnaround on approvals? And any guidance on cross-team coverage if multiple engineers are OOO?

Leila (People Ops): Managers should respond within 48 hours where possible. For coverage, follow the 'short-term staffing fallback' section: 1) post to the team rota channel, 2) ask the oncall/backup engineer, 3) if no internal coverage, request a temporary contractor through staffing-ops@redwood (priority path). We included an approval checklist in the doc.

Jin (Eng Manager): Got it. If it's a production incident and the person is needed, is there an expectation to deny the advance?

Priya (People Ops): Good q — safety-first. If denying would put someone at risk or violate leave law, default to approving and escalate staffing to eng-sre and product for triage. If it's a critical oncall gap, coordinate with eng-sre for temporary coverage.

Ava (Payroll): Note on payroll mechanics: employees choose between (a) recoup via reducing future PTO accruals over next 3 pay periods, or (b) one-time payroll deduction. International payrolls may have region-specific restrictions — payroll will reach out if there are constraints.

Sophia (Legal): Flag: for certain countries we can't do unilateral payroll deductions. People Ops will need explicit signed consent for option (b) in those regions — the doc lists affected countries.

Leila (People Ops): Correct — we added a region matrix and a sample consent form. Also added a short FAQ for managers on documentation needed for emergency leave.

Jin (Eng Manager): Thanks. Anything for travel-related sudden returns / rebookings? We had someone lose a flight and needed immediate time the other week.

Leila (People Ops): Travel disruptions: we added a travel-subsidy guideline — limited reimbursement for unavoidable extra costs tied to emergency leave (flights, one-night hotel) up to $500 for standard staffers. Submit receipts to travel-expenses@redwood with "PTO-ADVANCE" in the subject. Managers must pre-approve if possible.

Marcus (HRBP): Can managers approve extended advances (more than 5 days) in exceptional circumstances?

Priya (People Ops): Extended advances beyond 5 days require a level-2 review (People Ops + HRBP + manager). We included an escalation flow and timeline in the doc.

Oncall-bot: Reminder: for any approved PTO that impacts oncall rotation, managers must update the rota at least 24h before the start time or notify eng-oncall immediately.

Leila (People Ops): One last note — this is intended to be temporary while we pilot the approach for 6 months. We'll collect anonymized metrics on usage and any operational impact. Please read the full doc and use the request form: https://intranet.redwood/people/pto-request. If you have edge cases ping me or Marcus directly. :sparkles:

Jin (Eng Manager): Appreciate it — will share with my team today.

Ava (Payroll): We'll coordinate on the opt-in consent flows for international hires.

Marcus (HRBP): Thanks team — ping if you want a quick sync on the escalation flow.

Leila (People Ops): Thanks all! :heart:
